notes.atan2: y first: `atan2(y, x)` is the angle of the point (x, y), in (−π, π].
notes.clamp: As a constant's whole value it sets the slider's range: `a = clamp(0.4, 0, 1)` is a slider over [0, 1]. Anywhere else it is an ordinary function.
notes.interval: Every mention of one named interval is the same number; each written `interval(…)` is a separate one. In a tuple it traces like u and v: with one other parameter it fills a region, with two a solid. A list `[1..2]` is only the whole numbers 1 and 2.
notes.sort: Returns a tuple, which has an order and can be indexed: `sort(L)[2]`. A list `[ … ]` has none.
notes.hist: A whole row, not a value: the one thing to do to it is scale it, `hist(L, 40) / 800`.
notes.rotate: In 3D, `rotate(P, a)` turns about the z-axis; `rotate(P, a, axis)` about another.
notes.circle: Planar: in 3D, draw a circle as a parametric curve, `(cos(2pi u), sin(2pi u), 0)`.
notes.polygon: Fills in 2D. In 3D only triangles fill; a solid is `hull(…)` of its corners or a parametric solid.
notes.hull: Interior and repeated points are ignored; up to 2000 points in 3D. Flat 3D input draws a polygon.
notes.label: A whole row: `label((2, 4), "text")`, the text in quotes and a few words long. The point may use sliders and t.
notes.trail: The point must move with t, or be a state: a fixed point's trail is a dot.
notes.tube: The whole row, around a curve of exactly three components; an optional last argument is the radius (default 0.1).
notes.revolve: The whole row. The profile may use only its axis variable, sliders and t.
notes.action: A matrix alone on its row draws nothing; `action(M)` draws what it does.
notes.iter: Inside `iter` only, `z` is the iterate. With `w` (or x, y) in the step, iteration starts at 0 (the Mandelbrot set); with a constant step each point is its own start (a Julia set).
notes.domain: f is a complex expression in w, the point x + iy.
notes.conformal: f is a complex expression in w, the point x + iy.
notes.rgb: Channels run from 0 to 1, not 0 to 255. It fills the plane: to colour another row, end that row with a hex colour instead (`y = x^2 #e24`).
notes.sum: Bounds must be numbers or constants defined in another row (not t); a slider bound adds terms as it is dragged.
notes.int: The trailing `dx` names the variable. Alone on its row, a definite integral also shades the area it measures.
notes.curvature: Without u0 it is a function of u, for other rows: `(u, curvature(C))`. Alone on a row that is an error.
notes.frame: With t for u0 the frame rides along the curve: `C = (2cos(2pi u), sin(2pi u))`, then `C` and `frame(C, t/10)`.
notes.fourier: The signal runs over an interval, its period: `s = interval(0, 1)`, then `fourier(sin(2pi s))`. A signal in x is an error.
notes.open: The file stays on the device it was dropped on: a link carries its name and hash, not its data.
notes.graph: Cases in a graph row may test equality: `{mod(k, 2) = 0: k/2, 3k + 1}`.
notes.P: Needs a random variable declared in its own row: `X ~ Normal(0, 1)`, then `P(X < 1)`.
notes.E: Needs a random variable declared in its own row: `X ~ Normal(0, 1)`, then `E(X^2)`.

shapes.name: Circle
shapes.intro: The points at one distance, the radius, from a centre.

forms.note: centred at the origin

shapes.pitfall: centred elsewhere, `(x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = R^2`, or `circle((h, k), R)`.

shapes.name: Disc
shapes.intro: The inside of a circle, shaded.
shapes.pitfall: only in 2D. A solid in 3D is a ball.

shapes.name: Ellipse
shapes.intro: A circle stretched along its axes.

shapes.name: Parabola
shapes.intro: The graph of a quadratic: one bend, both arms rising (or falling) without bound.

forms.note: opens up for a > 0, down for a < 0
params: how steep; the vertex is the point (h, k)

forms.note: opening sideways

shapes.name: Hyperbola
shapes.intro: Two mirror-image branches that approach a pair of crossing lines, the asymptotes.

forms.note: branches left and right
params: the distance from the centre to each vertex, along x

forms.note: the rectangular hyperbola, its asymptotes the axes
params: how far out the branches sit (positive: first and third quadrants)

shapes.pitfall: swap the signs (`y^2/b^2 - x^2/a^2 = 1`) for branches above and below.

shapes.name: Cardioid
shapes.intro: A heart shape with a cusp: the path of a point on a circle rolling round another circle of the same size.

rows: (a(1 + cos(2pi u)) cos(2pi u), a(1 + cos(2pi u)) sin(2pi u))
forms.note: polar r = a(1 + cos θ), with θ = 2πu
params: the size; the curve reaches 2a along the positive x-axis, its cusp at the origin

rows: (2(1 + cos(2pi u)) cos(2pi u), 2(1 + cos(2pi u)) sin(2pi u))

forms.note: the same curve as an equation

shapes.pitfall: polar r = f(θ) is never a bare `r = …` row. With sin in place of cos the heart points up: r = a(1 + sin θ).

shapes.name: Limaçon
shapes.intro: The polar curve r = b + a cos θ: a dimpled oval, or a loop inside a loop when a > b. With a = b it is the cardioid.

rows: ((b + a cos(2pi u)) cos(2pi u), (b + a cos(2pi u)) sin(2pi u))
forms.note: polar r = b + a cos θ, with θ = 2πu
params: how much r swings; a > b makes the inner loop

rows: ((1.5 + 2.5cos(2pi u)) cos(2pi u), (1.5 + 2.5cos(2pi u)) sin(2pi u))
example.note: r = 1.5 + 2.5cos θ, with its inner loop

shapes.name: Rose
shapes.intro: Petals round the origin: the polar curve r = a cos(kθ) or r = a sin(kθ). An odd k gives k petals, an even k gives 2k.

rows: (a cos(2pi k u) cos(2pi u), a cos(2pi k u) sin(2pi u))
forms.note: polar r = a cos(kθ), with θ = 2πu
params: a whole number setting the petals

rows: (2cos(6pi u) cos(2pi u), 2cos(6pi u) sin(2pi u))

shapes.pitfall: kθ becomes 2πku, so r = sin(5θ) is `sin(10pi u)` inside both components. Polar is never a bare `r = …` row.

shapes.name: Lemniscate
shapes.intro: A figure eight lying on its side, crossing itself at the origin.

params: the half-width, where it meets the x-axis

rows: (a cos(2pi u)/(1 + sin(2pi u)^2), a sin(2pi u) cos(2pi u)/(1 + sin(2pi u)^2))
(2cos(2pi u)/(1 + sin(2pi u)^2), 2sin(2pi u) cos(2pi u)/(1 + sin(2pi u)^2))

shapes.name: Archimedean spiral
shapes.intro: A spiral whose turns are evenly spaced: r grows in step with θ.

rows: (a u cos(2pi n u), a u sin(2pi n u))
forms.note: polar r ∝ θ over n turns
params: the radius at the outer end

shapes.name: Logarithmic spiral
shapes.intro: A spiral whose turns widen by the same factor each time round: r = a e^(bθ).

rows: (a exp(2pi b n u) cos(2pi n u), a exp(2pi b n u) sin(2pi n u))
forms.note: polar r = a e^(bθ) over n turns
params: the growth rate; each turn multiplies r by e^(2πb)

rows: (0.2exp(0.9pi u) cos(6pi u), 0.2exp(0.9pi u) sin(6pi u))

shapes.name: Astroid
shapes.intro: A four-pointed star with curved sides, traced by a point on a circle rolling inside one four times its size.

params: the distance from the centre to each point
the distance from the centre to each point

shapes.pitfall: a fractional power of a negative number is undefined, so the equation needs `abs`.

shapes.name: Cycloid
shapes.intro: The arches traced by a point on the rim of a wheel rolling along the x-axis.

rows: (a(2pi n u - sin(2pi n u)), a(1 - cos(2pi n u)))
params: the wheel's radius; each arch is 2a high and 2πa long

shapes.name: Lissajous curve
shapes.intro: The path of a point swinging along x and y at two different frequencies.

rows: (sin(2pi a u + p), sin(2pi b u))
params: a whole number, the swings along x
a whole number, the swings along y; equal to a, it is only an ellipse

shapes.pitfall: multiply a component to stretch it: `(2sin(6pi u + 0.5), sin(10pi u))` is twice as wide.

shapes.name: Catenary
shapes.intro: The curve a hanging chain makes between two supports.

params: the height of the lowest point; larger a is flatter

shapes.name: Folium of Descartes
shapes.intro: A leaf-shaped loop in the first quadrant, its two tails running off along the line x + y = −a.

shapes.name: Helix
shapes.intro: A curve winding round a cylinder as it climbs.

rows: (R cos(2pi n u), R sin(2pi n u), h u)
forms.note: about the z-axis

shapes.pitfall: the third component must climb with u; `(cos(2pi u), sin(2pi u), 0)` is a flat circle.

shapes.name: Trefoil knot
shapes.intro: The simplest true knot: a closed curve in space that can't be untangled into a circle.

rows: (a(sin(2pi u) + 2sin(4pi u)), a(cos(2pi u) - 2cos(4pi u)), -a sin(6pi u))

shapes.pitfall: a 3D curve draws as a thin line; wrap it in `tube(…)` for a solid tube.

shapes.name: Plane
shapes.intro: A flat surface in 3D.

rows: a x + b y + c z = k
params: the x part of the normal (a, b, c)
the y part of the normal
the z part of the normal
where it sits: 0 passes through the origin

shapes.pitfall: a horizontal plane is `z = k`. In a 2D graph `x = 1` is a line, not a plane: some row must use z.

shapes.name: Sphere
shapes.intro: The points at one distance, the radius, from a centre in space.

forms.note: centred at the origin

rows: (R sin(pi v) cos(2pi u), R sin(pi v) sin(2pi u), R cos(pi v))
(1.5sin(pi v) cos(2pi u), 1.5sin(pi v) sin(2pi u), 1.5cos(pi v))

shapes.pitfall: centred elsewhere, `(x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 + (z - m)^2 = R^2`. `x^2 + y^2 = R^2` alone is a 2D circle.

shapes.name: Ball
shapes.intro: The solid inside a sphere.

rows: (s sin(pi v) cos(2pi u), s sin(pi v) sin(2pi u), s cos(pi v))
(s sin(pi v) cos(2pi u), s sin(pi v) sin(2pi u), s cos(pi v))

shapes.pitfall: `x^2 + y^2 + z^2 <= R^2` is an error: inequalities are 2D only. For the surface alone, see sphere.

shapes.name: Ellipsoid
shapes.intro: A sphere stretched along its three axes.

rows: (a sin(pi v) cos(2pi u), b sin(pi v) sin(2pi u), c cos(pi v))
(3sin(pi v) cos(2pi u), 2sin(pi v) sin(2pi u), 1.5cos(pi v))

shapes.name: Cylinder
shapes.intro: A tube of one radius around the z-axis.

rows: (R cos(2pi u), R sin(2pi u), h v)
forms.note: from z = 0 to z = h
endless along z

shapes.pitfall: without a z term, `x^2 + y^2 = R^2` is a 2D circle; `0z` makes it a surface.

shapes.name: Cone
shapes.intro: A surface whose radius grows in step with height, from a point, the apex.

forms.note: both nappes, the apex at the origin
params: the radius gained per unit of height

forms.note: the upper nappe only
params: the radius gained per unit of height

rows: (R v cos(2pi u), R v sin(2pi u), h v)
forms.note: one nappe, apex at the origin

shapes.pitfall: the equation in z^2 draws two cones tip to tip. For one, solve for z or use the parametric form.

shapes.name: Paraboloid
shapes.intro: A bowl: every horizontal slice is a circle, every vertical one a parabola.

params: how quickly it steepens; negative opens downward

shapes.pitfall: different coefficients on x^2 and y^2 make it elliptic, still a bowl. Opposite signs make a saddle.

shapes.name: Hyperbolic paraboloid
shapes.intro: A saddle: up along one axis, down along the other.

params: how slowly it rises along x
how slowly it falls along y

shapes.pitfall: `z = c x y` is the same saddle turned 45°.

shapes.name: Hyperboloid of one sheet
shapes.intro: A connected surface with a narrow circular waist that flares out above and below.

forms.note: about the z-axis
params: the radius of the waist, the circle at z = 0
the height scale: larger c flares more slowly

rows: (a cosh(2v - 1) cos(2pi u), a cosh(2v - 1) sin(2pi u), c sinh(2v - 1))

shapes.pitfall: one minus sign gives one sheet; two minus signs give two sheets. With no z term it is a cylinder.

shapes.name: Hyperboloid of two sheets
shapes.intro: Two separate bowls facing away from each other along the z-axis.

params: the height of each bowl's tip above or below the origin

shapes.name: Torus
shapes.intro: A ring-shaped surface: a circle swept round an axis it doesn't meet.

rows: (cos(2pi u)(R + a cos(2pi v)), sin(2pi u)(R + a cos(2pi v)), a sin(2pi v))
params: from the centre of the hole to the middle of the tube
the tube's radius, smaller than R

rows: (cos(2pi u)(3 + cos(2pi v)), sin(2pi u)(3 + cos(2pi v)), sin(2pi v))

params: from the centre of the hole to the middle of the tube

shapes.name: Möbius strip
shapes.intro: A band with a half twist: one side and one edge.

rows: (cos(2pi u)(R + h(v - 0.5) cos(pi u)), sin(2pi u)(R + h(v - 0.5) cos(pi u)), h(v - 0.5) sin(pi u))
params: the radius of the band's centre line

rows: (cos(2pi u)(2 + (v - 0.5) cos(pi u)), sin(2pi u)(2 + (v - 0.5) cos(pi u)), (v - 0.5) sin(pi u))

shapes.pitfall: the twist is `pi u`, half the turn `2pi u`.

shapes.name: Catenoid
shapes.intro: The surface of a catenary spun round the z-axis: the shape a soap film takes between two rings.

rows: (a cosh(h(2v - 1)/a) cos(2pi u), a cosh(h(2v - 1)/a) sin(2pi u), h(2v - 1))
params: how far it runs above and below the waist

shapes.name: Helicoid
shapes.intro: A spiral ramp: a line through the z-axis swept round as it climbs.

rows: (R(2v - 1) cos(2pi n u), R(2v - 1) sin(2pi n u), h u)
params: how far it reaches from the axis

shapes.pitfall: its edge is a helix; the helicoid is the surface.

shapes.name: Cube
shapes.intro: A solid box, or with equal sides, a cube.

forms.note: a corner at the origin
the convex hull of its 8 corners

shapes.pitfall: a box has its own interval per axis, e.g. `(interval(0, 1), interval(0, 2), interval(0, 3))`. `polygon` in 3D fills only triangles.

shapes.name: Tetrahedron
shapes.intro: The solid with four triangular faces.

forms.note: every other corner of a cube

example.note: the corner of a box, not regular

shapes.name: Octahedron
shapes.intro: The solid with eight triangular faces: two square pyramids base to base.
